spec_match.rationale: The decisive experiment: a frame genuinely named _current beside the linking frame, with a real link click deciding which one navigates — before/after semantics tabulated.

interactive.rationale: All three buttons work; the frame-state table reads the live tree via same-origin access.

blurb_alignment.rationale: One experiment separating the two behaviours, as the blurb promises.

edge_cases.rationale: Control click (ordinary name) included so the removal case has a baseline.

runtime_evidence.rationale: On this build the sibling named _current navigated — the after-the-removal behaviour — and the table said so; console clean.

accessibility.rationale: Same iframe-focus caveat as the sibling page; the page's own controls show visible focus.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite passes 4/4 on this build — the removal has shipped here, so _current resolves as an ordinary name.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; secondary buttons override both background and color.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 screenshots captured and inspected. The named-sibling experiment ran and showed the standard (post-removal) behaviour live.
